Implementation of CAS in metro cities  
*241. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of 
INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that recently, a final decision has been taken to implement 
the Conditional Access System in Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai; 
(b) if so, the details of the plan drawn up, including arrangements made for 
supply of Set Top Boxes, and the present status of its implementation; and 
2 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) the steps taken to launch any awareness campaign on the benefits of the 
CAS available to the consumers? 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI 
PRIYARANJAN DASMUNSI): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the 
House. 
Statement 
(a) Yes, Sir. CAS has been notified on 31st July, 2006 for implementation 
in parts of Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata, and the entire Chennai metropolitan area by 
31st December, 2006. 
(b) Vide this Ministry's GSR 452 (E) dated 31.7.2006 revised CAS Scheme has 
been notified under new rules 9 to 15 of Cable Television Network Rules, 1994. The 
amended rules and notification mentioned in (a) above are available on this Ministry's 
website www.mib.nic.in. The amended rules give the detailed scheme for 
implementation, roles assigned to various stakeholders, activity-wise time schedule, supply 
and installation of Set Top Boxes, safeguards to protect consumer interest amongst 
others. The notification and the time schedule are annexed. (Statement-I and II). 
(See below) 
(c) As provided in rule 12 of the amended rules a public awareness campaign 
among the subscribers in the notified areas will be launched for a period of thirty days 
from the date to be specified by Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), by the 
multi-system operators and may also include TRAI, the authorized offices or consumer 
organizations etc. The objective is to make the consumers aware of a-la-carte 
subscription rates for pay channels, rental scheme for Set Top Boxes, basic service tier, 
quality of service standards, subscriber management system, and dispute resolution 
arrangements among others. 
Statement-I 
NOTIFICATION OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND                  
BROADCASTING 
New Delhi, the 31st July, 2006 
G.S.R. 452(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clause (e) 
of sub-section (2) of section 22 of the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995 
(7 of 1995), the Central Government hereby makes the following rules further to amend 
the Cable Television 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
Networks Rules, 1994, namely:— 
1. Short title and commencement.—(1) These rules may be called 
the Cable Television Networks (Second Amendment) Rules, 
2006. 
(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the 
Official Gazette. 
2. In the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994, (hereinafter 
referred to as the principal rules), in rule 2,— 
(i) Clause (a) shall be renumbered as clause (aaaa) and before clause (a) as so 
renumbered, the following clause shall be inserted, namely:— 
"(a) "Act" means the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995 
(7 of 1995);". 
(aa) "Authority" means the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India 
established under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Telecom 
Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 (24 of 1997); 
"(aaa) "Broadcaster" means any person including an individual, 
group of persons, public or body corporate, firm or any organization or 
body who or which is providing programming services and includes 
his or her authorized distribution agencies," 
(ii) after clause (e), the following clauses shall be inserted, namely:— 
"(ee) "Multi-System Operator (MSO)" means a cable operator 
who receives a programming service from a broadcaster or his 
authorized agencies and re-transmits the same or transmits his own 
programming service for simultaneous reception either by multiple 
subscribers directly or through one or more local cable operators (LCOs), 
and includes his authorized distribution agencies by whatever name called; 
"(eee) "Notified area" means any area notified by the Central Government 
under section 4A of the Act;" 
4 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
2. In the Principal rules, in rule 7, after sub-rule (10), the following 
shall be inserted, namely:— 
"(11) No programme shall carry a dvertisements exceeding twelve 
minutes per hour, which may include up to ten minutes per hour of 
commercial advertisements, and up to two minutes per hour of a 
channel's self-promotional programmes." 
3. (i) in the principal rules, for rules 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14, the 
following rules shall be substituted, namely:— 
"9. Standard interconn ection agreements, tariffs and quality of 
service standards for the service providers in the areas notified 
under section 4A of the Act. —The Authority may, on issue of any 
notification under section 4A of the Act by the Central Government, 
take appropriate decisions on the following aspects and duly notify 
the— 
(a) standard interconnection agreement to be used for entering into 
commercial agreements for distribution in the notified areas, of pay or 
free-to-air channels among (i) broadcasters and multi-system operators; 
and (ii) multi-system operators and local cable operators; 
(b) the maximum limits of security deposit and monthly rental for 
supply, maintenance and servicing of set top boxes of prescribed 
specifications to the subscribers on rental basis by multi-system 
operators in the notified areas; 
(c) tariff for the basic service tier along with the minimum number of 
free-to-air channels to be provided by the multi-system operators 
or local cable operators to the subscribers in the notified areas; 
(d) regulations for quality of service to be provided by the multi-system 
operators or local cable operators to the subscribers in the notified 
areas; 
10. Nature and prices of channels.—(1) Every broadcaster shall declare 
the nature of each of its channels as 'Pay' or 'free-to-air' channel as well 
as the maximum retail price of each of its 'pay' channels to be charged 
by the multi-system operators or local cable operators from the 
subscribers in each of the notified areas. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
(2) Every broadcaster shall file his decl aration of the nature and prices 
of channels under sub-rule (1) before the Authority and the Central 
Government within fifteen days of the date of notification by the Central 
Government under section 4A of the Act. 
(3) If in the opinion of the Author ity, the price declared by the 
broadcaster in respect of any of its pay channels is too high, the 
Authority may, under section 11 of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of 
India Act, 1997 (24 of 1997), fix and declare the maximum retail price of 
such a pay channel or fix a general maximum retail price for all pay 
channels within which the broadcasters may declare their individual prices 
for each pay channel, to be paid by the subscribers in any of the notified 
areas, and such an order of the Authority shall be binding on the 
broadcasters and the multi-system operators and local cable operators. 
(4) Every broadcaster shall enter into interconnection agreements with 
multi-system operators in the notified areas as per the standard 
interconnection agreement, or with any mutually agreed modifications 
on a non-discriminatory basis, as per the regulations or directions or 
orders of the Authority. 
(5) If a broadcaster fails to declare the price of any of its pay channels within 
the prescribed time limit under sub-rule (2) of refuses or fails to comply 
with the direction under sub-rule (3) of refuses or fails to enter into an 
interconnect agreement with a multi-system operator permitted by the 
Central Government under sub-rule (3) of rule 11 within the time limit as 
prescribed by the Authority, then the Authority may, so as to protect the 
interests of the subscribers, take interim measures to ensure supply of 
signals. 
(6) In the event of non-compliance by the broadcaster of the 
directions issued by the Authority under sub-rule (5), the Central 
Government may, on the recommendations of the Authority, suspend 
the permission granted to the broadcaster under uplinking or 
downlinking guidelines as the case may be, to broadcast that 
channel in the country or any part thereof. 
(7) Every declaration filed by the broadcaster under sub-rule (1) or 
maximum retail price fixed by the Authority under sub-rule (3) shall 
normally remain valid for a period of one year from the date of such 
declaration or fixation, as the case may be, subject to the condition 
6 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
that every broadcaster will be free to revise the price of any channel or convert a pay 
channel to free-to-air or a free-to-air channel to a pay channel by giving one 
month's notice to the multi-system operator and subscribers: 
Provided that no increase in price beyond the individual limit, if any, 
specified by the Authority, shall be valid without prior approval of the Authority. 
Provided further that no such price increase shall be valid beyond the 
general maximum retail price for all channels fixed by the Authority. 
11. Grant of permission to multi-system operators to provide cable services with 
addressable systems in the notified areas:—(1) No multi-system operator shall 
provide cable television network services with addressable systems in any one for 
more notified areas without a valid permission from the Central 
Government under sub-rule (3) of rule 11. 
(2) Every multi-system operator who desires to provide cable 
television network services with addressable systems in any of the 
notified areas, shall within thirty days of the issue of the notifications 
under section 4A of the Act by the Central Government, apply for 
permission to the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting in Form 
6 annexed to these rules, alongwit h processing fee of rupees ten 
thousand. 
(3) The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting in the Government 
of India shall, within thirty days of the receipt of the application, 
grant, or refuse, permission to the applicant to provide addressable 
systems in the notified areas after considering its suitability or 
otherwise on the basis of information given in respect of its existing 
operators area, actual number of subscribers and addresses of its 
local cable operators in each of the notified areas, commercial 
arrangements with the broadcasters  and local cable operators, if 
any, financial strength, management capability, security clearance 
and preparedness to supply and maintain adequate number of set 
top boxes for its subscribers, installation of its subscriber 
management system and compliance with all other quality of service 
standards as may be specified by the Authority. 
7 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
(4) The Central Government may lay down such terms and conditions of 
permission under sub-rule (3) as may be deemed necessary and desirable to 
ensure compliance with the provisions of this Act and the regulations, directions 
and orders made by the Authority. 
(5) No multi-system operator shall continue to provide any cable television 
network services in the notified areas after the date notified therein, without 
obtaining prior permission from the Central Government. 
(6) In the event of a multi-system operator who fall or refuses to enter into an 
interconnection agreement with a broadcaster of a pay channel or an adequate 
number of local cable operators in the notified areas or who violate the terms 
and conditions of the permission granted to it under sub-rule (3), within the time 
limit as prescribed by the Authority, the Authority may, so as to protect the interests 
of the subscribers, take interim measures to ensure supply of signals. 
(7) In the event of violation by a multi-system operator of one or more of the 
terms and conditions of the permission granted under sub-rule (3), the Central 
Government may suspend or revoke such permission for such period and for such 
notified areas as it deems fit. 
Provided that no such order of suspension or revocation shall be made without 
giving reasonable opportunity to the multi-system operator to explain its 
position. 
12. Public awareness campaign about Conditional Access System Scheme—
(1) Every multi-system operator granted permission under sub-rule (3) of 
rule 11 shall create public awareness among the subscribers in the notified areas 
for a period of thirty days from the date to be specified by the Authority, either 
through advertisements in the print and electronic media or through other means 
(e.g. leaflets, printing on the reverse of the receipts, personal visits, group meetings 
with subscribers or consumer groups etc.) the salient features of the Conditional 
Access System scheme 
8 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
as approved by the Authority for implementation, by the multi system operator, in 
the notified areas, and in particular the following:— 
(a) A-la-carte subscription rates and the periodic intervals at which such 
subscriptions are payable for receiving the various pay channels; 
(b) The refundable security deposit and the daily or monthly rental payable for 
the set-top box and its detailed specifications such as make, model, technical

(c) The number and names of free-to-air channels that the multi-system 
operator will provide to the subscribers and specific placement of each

(d) The prescribed monthly service charge to be paid by each subscriber for

(e) The Quality of Service Standards specified by the Authority and the

(g) The subsisting arrangements for resolution of disputes between the multi-
system operator and local cable operators and the subscribers in respect of

(2) The Authority may also arrange public awareness activities in the notified 
areas either directly or through authorized officers or consumer organizations 
etc. 
13. Supply and Installation of Set Top Boxes:—(1) Every subscriber in 
the notified areas who desires to receive one or more pay channles shall, during 
the public awareness campaign under rule 12 or within fifteen days after its 
expiry, apply to any one of the 
9

multi-system operators granted permission under sub-rule (3) of rule 
11 either directly or through any of his linked local cable operators, to 
supply and install one or more set top boxes in his premises as per the 
scheme approved by the Authority and deliver the requisite channels 
through the same: 
Provided that every subscriber shall be free to buy a Set Top Box 
of approved quality from the open market, if available and technically 
compatible with the multi-system operator's system, and no multi-system 
operator or cable operator shall force any subscriber to buy or to take on 
rent the set top box from him only.

deliver the requisite channels through the same or through the set top box of

(3) Every multi-system operator shall procure, supply and install the 
required number of set top boxes of approved quality in the premises of every

own, as the case may be. 
(4) Every multi-system operator sha ll set up and operationalise its 
subscriber management system within a time frame as may be determined by 
regulation or order by the Authority, for ensuring efficient and error-free 
service to the subscribers by reco rding and providing individualized 
preferences for pay channels, billing cycles, refunds etc. 
(5) In the event of the failure of any multi-system operator to supply and 
install a set top box each in the premises of one or more applicants under sub-
rule (1) or to operationalise subscriber management system within the time 
limit as determined by regulation or order by the Authority,

then the Authority may, so as to protect the interests of the subscribers, take interim 
measures to ensure supply of signals. 
14. Dispute Resolution Mechanism — Every multi-system operator shall 
be obliged to maintain the quality of service as per the standards, including the 
arrangements for handling complaints and redressal of grievances of the subscribers, 
as may be determined by regulation or order by the Authority. The Authority may look 
into efficacy of such arrangements and issue necessary directions to the concerned 
parties for compliance. 
15. Transition to addressable systems. — (1) Immediately on 
operationalisation of the subscriber management system and the installation of the set 
top boxes under rule 13, every multi-system operator shall start transmitting the pay 
channels in encrypted as well as unencrypted form for a period of not less than fifteen 
days to test out the quality of service, remove any technical or operational snags and enable 
the subscribers to become familiar with the operation of addressable systems at their 
end. 
 
(2) Before the start of the transition period under sub-rule (1), the Authority may 
call for progress or compliance reports from the service providers in the Forms appended 
to these rules, and at intervals, as may be specified by it to satisfy itself that all the 
multi-system operators permitted under sub-rule (3) of rule 11 have completed all the 
necessary arrangements to switch over to transmission of pay channels through 
addressable systems in the whole of the notified areas by the date notified by the Central 
Government under section 4A of the Act. 
(3) In the event of satisfactory completion of all arrangements, every multi-system 
operator in the notified area shall start transmitting pay channels only through 
addressable systems from the date notified by the Central Government under section 
4A of the Act. 
(4) In the event of the Authority coming to a conclusion that the arrangements 
made by the multi-system operators are not adequate and the switch over to transmission 
of pay channels through addressable systems is likely to be against the interests of a 
substantial portion of the subscribers in any notified area, the Authority may 
recommend to the Central Government an extension of the notified date by such period 
as in its opinion is the minimum required for the satisfactory completion of the necessary 
arrangements by the multi-system operators.

SHRI PRIYARANJAN DASMUNSI: Sir, at that time, there was a serious 
hue and cry in the nation. Some were quoting the Set Top Box prices at Rs. 5,000 or 
Rs. 6,000, no support to repair or maintenance. All this forced, at that time, the 
subscribers to be on the streets in the metro cities and the Government of that day was 
not feeling proper to go ahead with that. Meanwhile, the court stay came and the 
people went to the court. Naturally, at that time, the whole scheme got on hold. 
When we took over the office, we tried to examine the whole parameter, how to 
protect the consumer, the subscriber, by providing cheaper rate. Therefore, Sir, 
we applied our mind in two ways. Way one, that a subscriber who does not want 
to enjoy a particular channel, it is being pushed on him by the cable operators in 
terms of the bouquet. The subscriber may have the choice of two channels, he is 
forced in the bouquet of five more other channels, which he does not want to watch. 
Then, the Ministry - of course, the previous Government also planned like that - 
found two ways. Way one, how much we can increase the DTH bouquets, which 
can be used by the subscriber without the cable operator. 'B', whether we can plan the 
CAS on the direction of the court, taking some more and more time to visualise and 
conceptualise the campaign of awareness among the subscribers in regard to the Set 
Top Box, in regard to the channel they like to use and in regard to the increasing of the Free-
to-Air channels. Unfortunately, when we planned this move, a few Free-to-Air 
channels were converted into pay channels. Even a foreign channel, the BBC World, 
it was a Free-to-Air channel, which got

converted into a pay channel. Then, Sir, we submitted before the court that if the pay 
channels get the access in the CA system and go to the subscriber's house, increasing 
the price, as they desire, will hit the people. So, we took two positions. Position one, the 
private channels or the pay channels cannot suo motu decide their prices without a 
detailed negotiation subjected to by TRAI and the deadline is 31st of August so that 
everybody knows transparently if I enjoy a 'y' channel, how much I have to pay. 
Accordingly, a subscriber will choose, I will select three channels and I will pay so 
much. So, it will be more transparent; and he will not be burdened with more 
channels. 
Secondly, Sir, with regard to the consumer burden, I can assure you, with all 
responsibility at my command, while implementing the CAS to the pay channels, I will 
ensure that the price we used to pay now is not a fixed price. Now, the cable operator's 
collection in these areas average from Rs. 150 to Rs. 300 per month from subscribers. 
In our case, when it will be implemented partially in parts of the cities of Delhi, 
Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata, it will be like this. 'A', if you take the Set Top Box at 
your house, you don't buy it. Pay a rent, a security deposit of Rs. 990 and then you pay 
Rs. 30 per months for the cable operator and you get the pay channels what you 
decide. But, the selected pay channels that you decide, those prices will be known to 
you only after 31st of August. We calculated it. In totality, he will pay much less than 
what he is paying now. But, Sir, there is a catch. The catch is that if the subscriber wants 
to buy the Set Top Box himself, it is up to him; but if he goes for security option and 
transfer the locality from South Delhi to West Delhi, then he can go to the MSO, who 
gave him the Set Top Box on rent, and return that box to him and take back the security 
deposit and go to other area and deposit it to the other MSO where his type of Set Top 
Box is being played. That hazard is still there. I don't deny this fact. But we can 
acclimatise the system properly after giving a trial for a year, and these hazards can be 
taken care of later on. But at the end of the day, the price to be paid by the subscriber 
depends on how many pay-channels he wants to watch. As I said, he should not bother 
about free-to-air channels. Set Top Box is not required for them.

CVC guidelines for organisations 
*246. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is mandatory for the organizations under the purview of Central 
Vigilance Commission to publish every month the summary of contracts/purchases made 
above a threshold value on their website; 
(b) whether most of such organizations are not displaying every month the 
summary of contracts/purchases made by them above a threshold value on their 
website; 
(c) if so, what action does the Central vigilance Commission propose to take in the 
matter; and 
(d) the details of the threshold value of each organization? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI SURESH PACHOURI): (a) to (d) A statement 
is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) As per CVC guidelines, all organizations within the purview of the CVC are 
required to post a summary every month of all the contracts/ purchases made above a certain 
threshold value to be decided by Chief Vigilance Officer in consultation with the Head of 
the Organization. 
(b) and (c) The Commission has observed that some organizations are not following 
the above guidelines and has directed all CVOs to ensure their implementation and to send 
monthly compliance report to the CVC in this regard. Whenever the CVO report non-
implementation by any organisation, the matter is suitably taken up with that 
organisation for implementation of the instructions. 
(d) Each organization has to determine its own threshold value, but as per the CVC 
guidelines it should cover more than 60% of the value of the transactions of an 
organization every month.

*248. SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRAP AL: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Wireless Planning and Coordination Cell have issued a circular for 
allotment of 5th and 6th criteria based on subscriber numbers; 
(b) whether it is a fact that subscriber-based allotment of spectrum is followed 
only in India and is not based on international norms; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that mobile operators are over reporting subscriber 
numbers; 
 
(d) if so, the reasons for adoption of this criteria and whether Government are 
taking any action to adopt a better method for spectrum allotment; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI DAYANIDHI MARAN): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid 
on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) The Order prescribing subscriber based criteria for allotment of 
5th and 6th CDMA carriers, subject to availability of spectrum, has been 
issued on 29th March, 2006. 
(b) Different countries follow diff erent criteria for allotment of 
spectrum. In India, availability of spectrum in the frequency bands, needed 
for the mobile telecom services, is constrained due to other existing 
operations and hence subscriber based criteria has been adopted for 
spectrum allotment to ensure efficient and optimal utilization of available 
spectrum. This method is considered to be the best suited at present for 
spectrum allotment in India. 
(c) The spectrum is needed for use by the. active subscribers and the amount of 
traffic generated by them. The recent Order of 29th March, 2006 concerning criteria 
for allotment of 5th and 6th CDMA carriers prescribes, inter alia, "Active 
Subscribers" averaged over a month in the Visitor Location Register (VLR) of the 
Network Management System (NMS). By this mechanism, over reporting is not 
possible. 
(d) Does not arise in view of (c) above. 
34 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
(e) As per the Order, only the active subscribers, who make and receive calls 
thereby generating traffic in the network, are taken into account for allotment of 
additional spectrum. The active subscribers in VLR and peak traffic in NMS, averaged 
over a month, are considered to be an objective mechanism for verification. 
SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRAPAL: Sir, while answering the question, in para

SHRI DAYANIDHI MARAN: Sir, there are constraints in allocation of 
spectrum, as the spectrum is used by various other Departments like Ministry of Space 
and Ministry of Defence. Basically, it is also given to other users much before the 
cellular service was started in our country. The moment we start the spectrum, we follow 
the international standards of spectrum. We are trying to make sure that these spectra are 
available and we use the international practices. 
SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRAPAL: Sir, in my question, I have 
specifically asked whether it is true that the mobile operators are over-reporting the 
number of subscribers. In the answer, the hon. Minister has tried to reply that there are

A subscriber is a subscriber. My specific question is: Is it true that the mobile operators are 
over-reporting to the Government about the number of subscribers? 
SHRI DAYANIDHI MARAN: Sir, the hon. Member has asked a very 
important question. The system is the international practice system where we monitor the 
number of subscribers. We have the system called "Home Location Register" and 
"Visitor Location Register". The Home Location Register is the system where anyone 
who buys a simcard is entered into the Register. But the Visitor Location Register is the 
Register system where the actual users, who use it, who are switching on the phone, 
will be registered. Those who have switched off the phone will not be included in that thing. 
The way the Department of Telecom is calculating the number of users is on the basis of 
the Visitor Location Register on an average of a month. You may use the phone today. 
Tomorrow, if you don't use it, in the record you wouldn't be registered as a user. 
We are following a

stringent method of Visitor Location Register where only active users are taken into 
consideration and the average of a month is taken. We are not taking into consideration the

doing that.

WLL system is expected to be slow in these areas.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI ANAND SHARMA): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
The Government on July 3rd, 2006 awarded a contract to transport and deliver 
to/from the airlines at the airport, closed and sealed diplomatic bags to a cargo handling 
company, M/s Dadson Global Cargo (Custom House Agent No. R093/98) for an initial 
period of six months. 
In view of tightened security requirement at the Indira Gandhi International 
Airport (IGI) requiring prior X-Ray, tagging before delivery and other documentation 
for both outbound/incoming consignments, it was decided that the transportation of 
diplomatic bags from South Block and Akbar Bhawan to IGI Airport for handing over to 
various airlines for onward carriage to Missions and receipt of incoming diplomatic 
bags would be better streamlined if given to a professional agency. It was also felt that a 
professional agency would be able to bring about a more efficient system as they would be 
better equipped to carry out the specialized job. There would be no security risk as the 
mandate of the firm would only be to transport and deliver to/from the airlines at the 
airport, closed and sealed diplomatic bags. After vetting of the draft contract by the Legal 
& Treaties Division of the Ministry and clearance from Internal Finance Division a 
limited tender (in view of the security and specialization requirement) was floated 
to 10 companies including Air India and Department of Posts. Department of Posts 
regretted their inability to handle the diplomatic bags outside the postal channel. Three 
companies, namely (i) M/s Dadson Global Cargo, D-229, Defence Colony, New Delhi (ii) 
K.L. Bhrara & Co. Pvt. Ltd., 42, Satya Niketan, New Delhi and (iii) M/s Mega Air 
and Sea Cargo, 204, 2 Community Centre, Phase-I, Naraina, New Delhi quoted for the 
limited tender. M/s Dadson Global Cargo was the lowest, at a figure of Rs. 14,40,000 
per annum, among the valid quotes. After receiving security clearance of M/s Dadson

SHRI ANAND SHARMA: Sir, as I have mentioned in the reply, this decision 
was taken after a careful consideration. As far as diplomatic bags are concerned, 
they are sealed bags which are sent from two location, namely from South Block 
and Akbar Bhawan. They are transported to the airports and carried then by the 
Airlines to their destinations. The diplomatic bags were earlier also, carried by the airlines. 
Regarding outsourcing, there are two factors which led to this decision. Firstly, we all 
know that the Screening Committee of the Government of India has recommended for 
abolition of certain jobs, as a result of which two-thirds of vacancies, which arise every 
year, are actually not available, in the sense that they are abolished. Now, two officers 
and four other employees had to be kept exclusively for transportation of bags. This 
again is a two-way process because diplomatic bags are not only set but they are also 
received. Every week about 600 bags are sent and 300 diplomatic bags are received 
from various destinations. Therefore, a decision was taken to outsource, of course, 
on a limited aspect. Now these are the sealed bags, which are security cleared, and 
which are delivered at the airports by the agency which has been hired for this 
purpose. As far as the security aspect is concerned, that has been fully taken into 
consideration. That is why there was a limited tender which was given only to those 
cargo handlers which had the experience, which was security cleared. Actually it is only 
after the Bureau of Security of the Ministry and al the security agencies cleared it that 
this decision was taken, and the contract has been fully vetted by the legal &

Increasing water crisis in Delhi 
*259. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH SHARMAH: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that acute water problem is increasing 
continuously in Delhi; 
70 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps that are being taken by Government to solve this problem? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI AJAY MAKEN): (a) and (b) The Delhi Jal Board (DJB) has 
informed that at present, demand of water for Delhi is about 900 million gallons per 
day (mgd). As against that, the total installed capacity for water treatment is of 650 
mgd. However, by optimizatipn of its plants, DJB is producing 675 mgd of potable 
water. Thus, there is a shorfall of 225 mgd. 
(c) The DJB has taken up the following steps to bridge the gap between 
demand and supply of water in Delhi:— 
(i) A 140 mgd Water Treatment Plant (WTP) has been set up in Trans Yamuna 
Area at Sonia Vihar. Based on the raw water drawn from the storage of the Tehri 
Dam in Uttaranchal, the trial run of the plant has commenced; 
(ii) A 40 mgd WTP has been set up at Nangloi. This plant is functioning at 
half of its capacity owing to raw water constraints. DJB is, therefore, pursuing 
with Government of Haryana to increase the supply of raw water for this 
plant; 
(iii) Construction of parallel lined channel from Munak to Hyderpur WTP has been 
taken up to reduce water losses due to seepage. This will augment water supply 
for Hyderpur WTP; and 
(iv) DJB has also taken up the works of recycling plants to treat backwash water 
and clarifloculator waste at Bhagirath (10 mgd capacity), Wazirabad (11 mgd 
capacity) and Hyderpur (16 mgd capacity) plants.

Speedy disposal of parcels 
1649. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state- 
83 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
(a) whether the Postal Department is taking steps for speedy disposal of 
parcles, money orders and letters; and 
(b) if so, the progress made as on date and by when these services are expected to 
be modernized in comparisons to the private courier service providers? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. 
SHAKEEL AHMED): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) Department of Posts is making consistent efforts to modernize postal services 
including parcel service, money order service and letter mail service. 
A separate parcel devision was set up in March, 2005 to provide a customer 
oriented approach with focus on management of all percel products and services 
including international parcels. 
To improve the quality of percel services, the Department under the 10th Five 
Year Plan, launched a scheme of setting up of Parcel Post Centres. 
A scheme of Establishment of International Parcel Post Hubs is being 
implemented under the 10th Five Year Plan. Mumbai Foreign Post Office, Delhi Foreign 
Post Office and Kochi Sub Foreign Post Office have been undertaken in this project. 
The Department of Posts has recently introduced an Instant Money Order (IMO) 
service in some selected cities, whereby money transfer can be effected instantly. 
Registered letters and high value money orders are being processed through 
Computerized Registration Centres, with a view to modernize the letter mail 
registration processing. As on date, 34 offices have been computerized. 
Automated mail processing centres have been set up at Mumbai and Chennai 
for processing of ordinary letter mail.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF

from ITI is proposed to be scrapped; 
(b) if so, the details in this regard; 
(c) whether incorporation of OEM clause in the tender regime has 
effectively barred ITI from contending for the BSNL supply orders even 
though ITI's quotation was most competitive; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether such measures are against the interest of ITI and are driving 
it towards closure; and 
112 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA

in communication sector and its survival against its overseas competitors in 
India? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. 
SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) and (b) No, Sir. Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) in its 
Management Committee Meeting on 12.07.2006 has decided to continue reservation 
quota to M/s ITI Ltd.

(OEM) clause in the tenders so that after sale services for the maintenance of the 
equipment so procured is assured. In one of the tenders, ITI could not meet the eligibility

Digital Device 
1661. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of COMMUNI 
CATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
113 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
(a) whether it is a fact that Qualcomm has recently told the 
Government that if the current spectrum policy remains unchanged, it will 
perpetuate over the long term a digital device in India by keeping consumers 
largely limited to voice service; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) what action Government propose to take in the matter? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. 
SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) M/s. qualcomm has stated, among others, that the current 
approach of spectrum assignment focu ses on voice services while limiting 
forward-looking operator's ability to  facilitate broad social benefit via 
broadband wireless data and information services. According to 
Qualcomm, this policy limits the present value of 3G capabilities in the 
Indian market and prevents service providers from offering broadband 
data services in rural markets despite availability of spectrum in these 
areas. Qualcomm has further said that the practical result of this policy, if 
maintained, is that it will perpetuate over the long term a digital divide in 
India by keeping Indian consumers on limited, voice-only 2g services 
while china, Europe and indeed, the rest of the world, move aggressively 
to advanced networks and a rich mix of compelling voice and data services 
based on 3G CDMA (CDMA 2000 and WCDMA). 
(c) The Spectrum Policy would take in to account all relevant aspects, 
as well as available technologies in this regard.

Permanent seat in UNSC 
1686. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTACHARJEE: Will the PRIME 
MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether further steps have been taken during the current year to 
secure its place in the UN Security Council as a permanent member with 
'Veto Power'; 
(b) if so, results thereof; and 
(c) the permanent UN Security Council, members and other that have 
so far come out in support of India's claim? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI ANAND SHARMA): (a) to (c) The Government continues to 
actively pursue India's candidature for a permanent seat of the UN Security 
Council. Further steps in this regard were taken by the Government during the 
current year. The Framework Resolution of the G-4 countries (India, Brazil, 
Germany and Japan), which had been introduced by the G-4 during the last 
(59th) Session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA), was re-tabled during the 
current (60th) Session of UNGA by India, Brazil and Germany. Japan has been 
positively involved in the G-4 consultations before as well as after the re-
tabling of this Resolution. The Government has also continued to utilise bilateral 
meeting with different countries to  mobilise further support for India's 
candidature, besides participating actively in the debates of Security Council 
reform at the United Nations. Support for India's candidature, which has been 
steadily increasing, has been expressed in various forms and fora. Some 
countries have expressed support confidentially in bilateral discussion with 
Government of India. 
As regards the issue of 'Veto Power', India believes that the existing and 
new permanent members of the Security Council should have same 
137 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
responsibilities and rights. This principle is underlined in the G-4 Framework 
Resolution. However, based on extensive consultations and keeping in view the 
wide divergence of views on the issue of Veto, the G-4 Resolution provides 
for a decision on this issue at a review which is envisaged 15 years after the 
entry into force of the amendments to the UN Charter for the expansion of the 
Security Council.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI 
M.V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a) and (b) The Planning Commission estimates the 
incidence of poverty at national and state level from the large sample survey on 
household consumer expenditure conducted by the National Sample Survey 
Organisation (NSSO) at an interval of approximately five years according to the 
Expert Group Methodology (Lakdawala Committee on Estimation of Proportion and 
Number of Poor). The latest available data from such surveys in from NSS 55th Round, 
which was conducted in 1999-2000. The next estimates of poverty will be based on the 
61st round of NSSO, (July 2004 to June 2005), the results of which have not been 
published. The percentage of people living below the poverty line using data from the 
quinquennial rounds of National Sample Survey Organisation on household consumption

1727. SHRI MAHENDRA M OHAN: Will the Minister of SHIPPING,

upgrade over 100 non-major ports in the country to handle 
182

large vessels, with a view to enhancing the country's port capacity from 600 million 
tonnes to 2000 million tonnes;

THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. BAALU): (a) to (c) There are 187 ports other than major 
ports (non-major ports) which are under the overall jurisdiction of the respective State 
Governments/Union Territory Administrations. During an interactive session on the Port 
Sector between the Department of Shipping and port authorities in the Maritime State 
Government and Union Territory Administrations held on 3rd July, 2006, a scenario 
where the Indian ports, both major and non-major, need to plan for building up an 
aggregate capacity of at least 2000 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) by the year 2016-17

in the near future. Responsibility for the development and augmentation of capacities in 
the non-major ports devolves on the respective State Governments/Union 
Territory Administrations.

203 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
The State Government proposal consists of two parts, namely, Mumbai 
Sewage Disposal Project Stage-ll for US$ 432 million and Slum Sanitation 
Programme of US $ 110. million. Components under the Mumbai Sewage 
Disposal Project Stage-ll are rehabilitation of Sewers and manholes, diversion 
of all illegal connections (house connections discharging to storm water drains 
or nallahs) to the foul sewer system, provision of new and up-sized sewers to 
carry predicted flows, remedy of problems at the pumping stations, 
replacement of old pumps and equipments, modification of the treatment 
works, etc. The areas to be covered under Sewerage Works include Colaba, 
Worli, Bandra, Versova, Malad, Bhandup & Ghatkopar. 
Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project St age-ll was recommended to Deptt. 
of Economic Affairs for financial assistance through World Bank in the year 
2004. The State was, however, categorized as 'debt stressed' State from debt 
sustainability point of view. Accordingly, the Deptt. of Economic Affairs 
informed that since Maharashtra is a debt stressed State, these proposals 
could not be forwarded to the World Bank. 
In addition to above, Deptt. of Economic Affairs also informed that in 
November, 2004, Chief Minister of Maharashtra requested for engaging the World 
Bank to prepare a five year business plan for transforming Mumbai into a world 
class city and to include Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project Stage-ll in the 
comprehensive plan for the city. Subsequently, Deptt. of Economic Affairs 
requested the World Bank of February, 2005 to field a dedicated multi-sectoral 
team to draft a comprehensive strategy for the city. 
The World Bank teams visited Mumb ai twice last year and held 
extensive discussion with officials of Government of Maharashtra and with 
Task Force, appointed by the Chief Minister for preparing an Action Plan to 
develop Mumbai into a world class city. The World Bank team, which visited 
Mumbai from 8th to 21st November, 2005, has proposed a time schedule for 
Action Plan preparation relating to the Mumbai Development Action Plan. 
The proposed Action Plan involves action by State Government on a 
comprehensive package of key reforms, investing and financing. As per time 
schedule, prepared by World Bank, the Action Plan is expected to be launched 
in December, 2006. The State Government  has been requested to adhere to 
the time schedule. The likely estimated expenditure to be spent on the project 
will be available on finalisation of 'Action Plan'.

(b) The programme involved 900 artistes drawn both from India and the Indian 
community resident in Melbourne and surrounding areas. The programme included a 
multifaceted presentation of various Indian art and culture forms, supplemented by an 
audio-visual presentation of different parts of Delhi and India. Leading film artistes, 
including, Ms. Aishwarya Rai, Shri Saif Ali Khan and Ms. Rani Mukherjee participated in 
the event. 
(c) No specific budget provision was made for the participation of the Indian 
Contingent for the Commonwealth Game; the expenditure is likely to be about Rs. 2.87 
crores. These Games are funded from the Scheme of Assistance to National Sports 
Federations which caters to the various activites related to promotions of Sports. The 
expenditure on the participation of Indian contingent includes ceremonial kit, out of pocket 
allowance, to and fro airfare, uniform, etc. 
(d) As indicated above, the funds for the Indian cultural segment at the closing 
ceremony were provided by Government of NCT of Delhi. The funds for participation 
of Indian contingent in the Commonwealth Games, 2006 were provided by the 
Government of India from — "Demand

Delegation to Melbourne 
1789. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have sent any delegation to Melbourne to 
acquire first hand knowledge in view of Commonwealth Games at Delhi in 
2010; 
(b) whether the delegation has submitted any report to Government; and 
(c) if so, the reaction of Government thereon? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI 
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) Delegations of agencies concerned with the 
preparation for the Commonwealth Games, 2010 (CWG 2010), namely, the 
Sports Authority of India, the Government of NCT of Delhi, the Delhi 
Development Authority and CPWD have visited Melbourne. The Organising 
Committee have also deputed secondees and observers drawn from different 
departments and disciplines. In addition, an official delegation was deputed by 
the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in two batches to witness and observe 
the Melbourne Games. 
(b) and (c) Officials of CPWD and DDA have submitted their reports to 
their respective administrative Ministries. SAI have submitted a detailed report to 
this Ministry containing observations, comments and recommendations 
relevant to the organization of CWG 2010. Based on the studies undertaken by 
delegations, inputs have been obtained for plans for sports venues, 
infrastructure and management to be developed by these agencies for CWG 
2010. 
Poor performance by India in Sports events 
1790. SHRI DARA SI NGH: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have taken any steps to find out the reasons for 
poor performance of India in the Athens Olympic Games and other International 
events; 
234 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Sports Authority of India is responsible for the poor 
performance of India to some extent, if not, on whom the responsibility has 
been fixed, till date; 
(d) whether Government have increas ed budgetary allocations during 
2006-07 on sports for providing international standard training facilities, diet, 
scientific support, high standard coaching by foreign and Indian coaches, etc.; 
and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI 
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) and (b) While it is fact that there is considerable room 
for improvement on the standard of sports in the country, the fact is that the 
performance of Indian sportspersons has been steadily improving. At the 
Commonwealth Games 2002 held in Manchester, India secured the fourth 
position and won 69 medals, as against 25 medals won by Indian participants in 
the earlier Commonwealth Games in Kuala Lumpur. In the Commonwealth 
Games held at Melbourne in 2006, Wrestling and Judo were not included and 
the number of medals available in the Weightlifting discipline had been 
significantly reduced; in all these disciplines India could have secured medals. 
Notwithstanding this reduced number of medals available for India in the 
Melbourne Games, India retained its fourth position. Indian sportspersons 
have performed creditably in a number of international competitions 
including the First Afro-Asian Games in Hyderabad and SAF Games in 
Islamabad in 2004. In the Athens Olympics 2004, India won the first ever Silver 
medal in an individual event since Independence while some of the 
sportspersons gave their best performances. In the Paralympic Games 2004 at 
Athens, India won 1 gold medal in athletics and 1 bronze medal in power- 
lifting. 
Recently many Indian sportspersons have excelled at the world level. A 
few outstanding achievements of the Indian sportspersons are as under:— 
1. Indian Archers have won the Silver Medal at the recent World 
Championship. 
2. Indian Shooters have won many medals at Shooting World 
Championships, including three gold medals by individual Shooters 
235 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
(2 Seniors & 1 Junior) at the recently concluded Zaghreb World 
Shooting Championship. 
3.     Billiards and Snookers — our players have won the World 
Championships in the last two years. 
(c) Sports is a State subject and its promotion at the State level is 
the responsibility of the State Governments concerned. However, the 
Government of India, through its own Schemes and the Schemes of the 
Sports Authority of India (SAI), augments the efforts of the State 
Government for improving sports performance at the Junior, Sub-Junior 
and Senior Levels. 
The preparation and training of sportspersons for major international events, 
including the Commonwealth Games, is an on-going process which takes into 
account inputs provided by National Sports Federations. A systematic approach 
is adopted to the selection and training of athletes and teams for participation in 
major international events by drawing up and implementing four-year roll-on 
Plans within the frame work of Long Term Development Programmes 
(LTDP) under which exceptionally talented sportspersons, selected on the 
basis of their performance, are put through scientifically designed continuous 
training programmes. 
(d) and (e) The Sports-related budget allocation of this Ministry with 
reference to the schemes of the Sports Authority of India, Talent Search 
and Training and Assistance to National Sports Federations under which 
international training facilities, diet, scientific support, high standard 
coaching by foreign and Indian coaches, etc. are covered, has increased 
from Rs. 174.81 crore during 2005-06 (RE) to Rs. 193.06 crore during 
the year 2006-07 (BE). 
National Youth Policy 
1791. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to review "India's National Youth 
Policy" formulated in 2003; 
(b) if so, the steps Government have taken so far to ensure all round 
development of youth in the country so as to fulfill their legitimate aspirations 
particularly in the age group of 13 to 19 years; and 
(c) whether Government have accorded any priority to rural and 
236 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
tribal youth, female adolescents, youth with disabilities and victims of 
trafficking, orphans etc., please give details? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI 
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The Government has recognized youth belonging to the age group 
of 13-19, which is a major part of the adolescent age group, as a separate 
constituency. Further, the Ministry is implementing a 100% central sector 
scheme of financial assistance for the Development and Empowerment of 
Adolescents. 
(c) Yes, Sir. Apart from various schemes of the Ministries of Women & 
Child Development, Health and Fam ily Welfare and Social Justice and 
Empowerment for out of school girls and female adolescents, destitute women 
(including victims of trafficking), adolescent health, persons with disabilities 
(including youth) etc., due representa tion is accorded in the youth related 
programmes of this Ministry to tribals, out of school youth, under privileged 
sections of society, including SCs and STs, and women. The Nehru Yuva Kendra 
Sangathan, an autonomous organization of the Ministry, works for the 
empowerment, welfare and development of rural youth through its large 
network of Nehru Yuva Kendras in the country.

1792. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have any plans to encourage and find talent 
for games like football and volleyball; 
(b) if so, the steps that are being taken to extend assistance directly to 
educational institutions to foster talent; 
(c) the steps proposed by Government to find ways to encourage talent; 
(d) whether Government have plans to extend financial assistance for this 
proposal to encourage popular and low-cost games like football and volleyball; 
and 
(e) the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI 
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) The development of sports, including the scouting 
237 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
and nurturing of talent in various sports disciplines, is primarily the 
responsibility of the State Governments and the National Sports Federation (NSF) 
concerned. However, the Government of India supplements the efforts of the 
NSFs in various sports disciplines, including football and volleyball, by 
providing financial assistance for purchase of equipment, scientific support and 
training by Indian and foreign coaches, participation in international events 
abroad, holding of international & national tournaments in the country, 
sending teams abroad for training-cum-participation in international 
tournaments etc. 
(b) to (e) Till 1.4.2005, Government of India, under the scheme for 
Grants to Rural Schools for Purchase of Sports Equipments and Development 
of Playfields was giving assistance directly to schools situated in rural areas, 
and also to colleges and universities directly for non consumable sports 
equipments and sports infrastructure. Both these sub-schemes have been 
transferred to the State sector with effect from 1.4.2005. 
However, Government of India is implementing various other schemes 
to provide incentives for the promotion of sports activities and assistance to 
sportspersons. These include schemes for assistance through the Sports 
Authority of India for organizing tournaments at various levels under the 'Rural 
Sports Programme' and 'Promotion of Sports and Games in Schools', the scheme 
for pensions to meritorious sportspersons/ medal-winners in international events 
after their retirement from active sports career through the Sports Fund, 
assistance to sportspersons of yesteryear living in indigent conditions through the 
National Welfare Fund, and assistance to promising sportspersons through the 
National Sports Development Fund.

RULING BY THE CHAIR 
Rejection of Shri Natwar Singh's privilege motion against Prime 
Minister, Dr. Manmohan Singh 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I have received a notice, dated the 4th 
August, 2006, from Shri Natwar Singh, wherein he has stated, inter alia, that 
within a few minutes of the submission of the Pathak Commission's Report to 
the Prime Minister the main findings of the Report were made available to the media; 
that the Report had neither been shown to him nor a copy of it was laid on the 
Table of Rajya Sabha. He has, therefore, requested that under Rule 188 of the 
Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha, he be allowed to 
raise this matter of breach of privilege of the House. 
As the House is aware, Justice R.S. Pathak Inquiry Authority was 
appointed by the Government on the 11th November, 2005. The Government 
laid the Report of this Authority, along with Action Taken Report, on the table of 
the House on the 7th August, 2006. The Report of the Authority had been 
presented to the Government on the 3rd August. It is sad as well as unfortunate 
that some contents of the Report came to be known to the media that very day. It 
would have been appropriate and desirable that when Parliament was in 
session, no part of the Report should have become public before it was 
presented to Parliament. This is definitely a serious matter which needs to be 
looked into and investigated. However, this matter, though very unfortunate 
and deplorable, does not involve the question of any breach of privilege of the 
House. Past precedents in similar cases also lead me to reach the decision 
that this matter does not constitute any  breach of privilege of the House. I 
accordingly hold that the said notice is not admissible. Now, Special Mentions.

Concern over huge backlog of cases in various 
courts in the country—(Contd.) 
SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Sir, it  is stated that 1.62 crore cases 
are pending in different courts, of which 1.18 crore are pending in magisterial 
courts. Thousands of people are said to be languishing in various jails awaiting 
trials. Such gigantic backlog is primarily attributed to the woeful lack of judicial 
officers at various levels. Poor infrastructure and facilities in the courts further 
compound the situation, which is more pathetic at the district level courts. It 
calls for concerted effort from all conc erned to find a solution to the gigantic 
problem. 
The excruciating delay in settlement of court cases is a matter of great 
concern to the litigants as also to the Judiciary and the Government. Cases filed 
decades ago still remain to be settled. Though the people have not lost hope in 
the Judiciary and its ability to render justice, a sense of despondency nevertheless 
takes over and lends credence to the age-old adage, 'justice delayed, justice 
denied.' 
A beginning should be made by improving the infrastructural facilities in all 
courts. Towards this objective, the Centre should allocate, at least, Rs. 3000 
crores. The Bar Associations, the J udiciary and the Government should 
endeavour to hasten the process of litigation. The Government could consider 
setting up fast track courts and introducing enhanced working hours or shift 
system at all courts. 
All this is to be done for sustaining the hope and confidence of the people 
in these temples of justice.

SHRI C. PERUMAL (Tamil Nadu): Sir, the Integrated Coach Factory was set up

coaches in a year. Another coach factory was set up at Kapurthala in Punjab a few 
years back, but that factory is producing 1500 coaches a year.

increased. There is always an acute shortage of railway coaches in our country. With

GOVERNMENT BILLS 
The Actuaries Bill, 2006 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
PAWAN KUAMR BANSAL): Sir, I beg to move: 
"That the Bill to provide for regulat ing and developing the profession of 
Actuaries and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, as passed by 
Lok Sabha, be taken into consideration." 
Sir, in simple terms, an actuary is a person skilled in determining the 
present effect of future contingent events. The Actuarial Society of India, which 
is there at Bombay, was registered under the Bombay Public Trust Act and the 
Societies Registration Act. So far, only 203 members of the ASI are entitled to 
practise, and out of them, only 137 are in the country, while 66 are outside the 
country. 
Sir, with the expansion of economic activity, particularly that in the 
Insurance sector, it has been felt that there is greater need for the actuaries to really 
take up various works assigned to them. As such, Government has come up 
with this Bill. This Bill was referred to the Standing Committee. The Standing 
Committee deliberated at length on this Bill, made certain worthwhile 
suggestions, including one relating to the definition of the actuary itself. We 
have incorporated those amendments in the Bill. The Bill was passed by the Lok 
Sabha and that is how we are here before you. 
Sir, this Bill, on the lines of  the laws governing the Company 
Secretaries, the Chartered Accountants and the Cost and Works Accountants, 
takes into consideration the need to regulate this profession now. Earlier, because 
of the restrictive practice, as you would appreciate, Sir, there was very limited role 
for the actuaries as such. But, today, the 
259 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
Insurance sector is growing up and the need of actuaries is being felt in many 
areas. Hence, it was felt that instead of the Society registered under the Societies 
Registration Act, there is need to have an Institute of Actuaries, and also, to 
provide for various provisions governing their profession as such. 
Sir, this Act deals with the incorporat ion of the institute of Actuaries, the 
composition of the Council of the Institute, which would manage the affairs of 
the Institute. It deals with general meetings, elections to the Council, 
establishment of tribunal to deal with matters of dispute relating to the elections 
of the Institute; committees of the Council to deal with various matters including 
disciplinary matters, etc. In any profession, the need to maintain high standards 
of professional conduct is of the utmost importance and that care has been taken 
here in this Bill. The Schedule contains a list in detail about what could be 
professional misconduct. So, there are provisions in the Bill, which deal with 
cases of misconduct through the Disciplinary Committee. There is provision to 
appoint a Prosectution Director, who, along with other employees, could assist 
the Disciplinary Committees about various matters which come up before the 
Disciplinary Committee. 
Sir, there is provision for an Appellate Authority, for matters to be finally 
decided there. This Appellate Authority would be the one which is there for the 
Chartered Accountants also, excepting with the change that when it deals with 
matters relating to the Actuaries, it would be the Actuaries who will replace the 
Chartered Accountants, or, for that matter, the Cost and Works Accountants. It is 
because there is not much work before the Appellate Authority as such that a 
common authority with the necessary changes has been provided for. There is 
also a provision for establishment of the Qu ality Review Board. It is felt that to 
achieve the best world practices in this profession, there is a need to have a 
Quality Review Board which would consider matters from time to time, and then 
lay down that as to what are the best practices, what quality has to be 
maintained and that has been provided for. This Bill has received unanimous 
and all round support from Members of the Lok Sabha and in the other House. I 
urge upon the hon. Members here also to take the Bill into consideration and 
ultimately pass it.

MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR (Orissa): Si r, Jamadarpali airstrip in 
Sambalpur, Orissa, is in a shambles. Built during the construction of Hirakud 
Dam, it provides landing facilities for officials visiting Sambalpur, Hirakud and the 
nearby districts. This airstrip gained greater significance after Jharsuguda 
aerodrome was declared unsafe.

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
The airstrip is being misused, as there is,no proper security and fencing. Loaded 
commercial vehicles often ply across the runway damaging the surface. The 
greenery near the airstrip has become a grazing ground for the cattle which has 
damaged the black topping and the landing area of about 18,970 sq. metres.  
The airport has emerged as a necessity, considering various factors. The Sambalpur-
Rengali-Jharsuguda corridor is fast turning into a growth corridor of the State. Apart from 
global scale plants by Aditya Birla, Sterlite Industries, Bhusan Steel, Reliance Energy and

headquarters of PSU, Mahanadi Coal Fields Ltd., Sambalpur Railway Division, LIC 
Division, Sambalpur University Engineering Colleges and Medical Colleges, and the 
world famous Hirakud Dam are located in and around Sambalpur. 
Realising the importance of the airport, the State PWD authorities have prepared 
proposals for its renovation. Once repaired, the airstrip will help boost the economy of 
this region. 
As this august House is aware, Orissa is the most backward and a cash-strapped 
State. The Centre should, therefore, help the State Government both financially and 
physically to develop this airport to improve the economy of this region.

Concern over mismanagement in the Hindustan Teleprinters 
Limited 
SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA (Tamil Nadu): Sir, the Hindustan Teleprinters Limited 
was established way back in 1962 as a Public Sector Undertaking. This 
establishment has been manufacturing Electro Mechanical Teleprinters and 
National Internet Backbone, and BSNL was the major customer for the HTL. 
This organisation has been a profitmaking one till the year 2001, and had paid a 
dividend of Rs. 90.00 lakhs to the Central Government in the year 2001. 
However, the then Government sold 74 per cent of the Government's equity to 
the Himachal Futuristic Communications Ltd., a company which was involved 
in share-market scandal. The then Gove rnment declared the value of assets 
of the company at Rs. 55.00 crores, and took Rs. 38.00 crores. After the new 
management under Himachal Futuristic Communications took over the 
establishment, salaries to the employees were never paid on time. And, 
moreover, statutory payments, such as, PF, LIC, PLI, Gratuity, Group 
Insurance, etc., have not been paid by the new management. These statutory 
payments amount to crores of rupees, when this new man agement took over 
the HTL, within a span of six months, they brought

the profit making company in to a loss making unit and for the year 2001-02 they 
declared a net loss of Rs. 107.00 cror es. The company made profit in the 
preceding year, but, they branded this company as a sick unit, and the matter 
is before the BIFR. The new management had promised, at the time of signing 
of an agreement with the Government, t hat they will invest Rs. 20.00 crores. 
However, they have not invested even a single rupee, whereas they collected 
the outstanding amount of about Rs. 600.00 crores from the customers, and 
had also received a sum of Rs. 29.62 crores from the National Highway Authority 
for the land given to the NHAI. Now, the future of about 650 employees working 
in this organisation is at stake. Therefore, I urge upon the Government to 
intervene in the matter and bring back this unit again as a Public Sector 
Undertaking or merge this unit with the BSNL. 
Need to take steps for the Welfare of Minority Community in 
Murshidabad, West Bengal 
SHRI MOINUL HASSAN (West Bengal): Sir, Murshidabad, in West 
Bengal is a minority community-based di strict. Nearly 63 per cent of the 
population is the minority community, mainly Muslims. Education is one of the 
major problems among them. 
Recently, children from the Muslim community are coming to schools and 
colleges. The Government should provide some special programmes for the 
development of the minority community in that particular district. I would like to 
request the Government of India to provide help to this district through the 
State Government to establish a medical college and an engineering college, 
which will improve the present education status of the community. A lot of girls 
are coming in educational institutions for their higher education. But they are 
facing accommodation problems in the town area. 
I urge upon the Government to give more attention in this field, which 
will help the common people of our country. A large section of this community is 
engaged in weaving. But the present situation of this section is that it is going to be 
ruined. Without the proper help of the Government of India, it is not possible to 
survive in the present situation. I urge upon the Government to look into the 
matter.

STATEMENT BY MINISTERS 
Issue of Pesticide contamination in soft drinks 
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (SHRI DINESH TRIVEDI): Dr. Ramdoss to make a 
statement on the issue of pesticide contamination in soft drinks. 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI 
RAMDOSS): Sir, the Centre for Science and Environment, New Delhi released a 
Press Report on 2nd August, 2006 on their website, in the print media as well as electronic 
media about the studies carried out by them on the presence of pesticide residues in 
carbonate beverages. The CSE in their report have stated that during 2006 they have 
analysed 57 samples of 11 soft drink brands, from 25 different manufacturing plants of 
Coca-Cola and Pepsi Co., spread over 12 States. These samples were lifted by the CSE 
from September 2005 to March 2006. The CSE study finds pesticide residues in all 
samples. 
310 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
The CSE has found pesticide residues of organo chlorine pesticides (HCH and its 
derivatives and Heptachlor) and organo phosphorous pesticides (Chlopyrifos and 
Malathion) in the soft drink samples tested and analysed by them. 
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has taken note of the studies 
carried out by the CSE as well as its discussion in the print and the electronic 
media on 2nd August, 2006. The CSE has made available a copy of the 
aforesaid study entitled "Soft Drinks-Hard Truth 11", to the Ministry on 
04.08.2006. The report of the CSE is being examined. 
I would like to inform the House that  the standards for soft drinks or 
"carbonated water" were formula ted under the Prevention of Food 
Adulteration Rules, 1955 in the year 1955 for the first time and have been 
subsequently amended from time to time. These standards for soft drinks have 
provided that the water to be used in making carbonated water should conform 
to the standards prescribed for packaged drinking water. These standards also 
provide microbiological requirements, maximum metal contaminants and 
declaration of added sugars, various food additives including caffeine, artificial 
sweeteners and food acids. 
The CSE published another report in the year 2003 on pesticide 
residues in soft drinks. The matter relating to pesticide residue in soft drinks 
was examined by a Joint Parliamentary Committee headed by Shri Sharad 
Pawar. It was brought out by the JPC that soft drinks consisted of the following 
ingredients:— 
1. Water comprising 86-92 per cent of total volume 
2. Sugar comprising 5-10 per cent of total volume 
3. Concentrate 
4. Ingredients other than concentrate which include carbon dioxide, acids 
such as citric acid, phosphoric acid and malic acid. 
The JPC in its report at Para 2. 179 has reported that due to the 
manufacturing process, pesticide resid ues are not substant ially contributed 
from sugar. The observations of the JPC are as follows:— 
"2.179 Carbonated water manufacturers have already mentioned before 
JPC that they have foolproof process to select and treat the sugar 
311 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
and this treatment is uniform worldwide to ensure good quality sugar syrup for 
the products. These companies are already purifying the sugar syrup with Hot 
Carbon Treatment Process, which is effective in reducing most of the pesticide 
residues to below detectable level or below 0.1 ppb levels. The Committee feels 
that sugar, therefore, cannot be the only source of pesticide residues." 
Regarding the concentrate used by the manufacturer in these products, 
the manufacturers stated that the quality of concentrate used in these products 
are the same as used in other countries around the world and in addition to the 
concentrate, the food additives used in these products also meet all statutory 
requirements. 
The JPC in its recommendation number 2.181 has recommended as 
follows:— 
"...The Committee, therefore, recommend that standards for carbonated 
beverages, which are best suited for the Indian conditions need to be fixed in 
the overall perspective of public health. These standards should also be 
stringent enough. The reason that the other countries have not fixed such limits 
should not dissuade our law makers in attempting to do so, particularly when a 
vulnerable section of our population who are young and constitute a vast 
national asset are consuming the soft drinks. In the Committee's view, therefore, it 
is prudent to seek complete fr eedom from pesticide residues in sweetened 
aerated waters. 'Unsafe even if trace' should be the eventual goal." 
[MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair] 
"The Committee are, therefore, of the considered opinion that the water 
used in manufacturing the soft drinks should be in conformity with the new 
norms which have already been notified under Notification No. GSR 554(E) 
dated 18.7.2003 so that the consumers are not deprived of the best standards." 
Sir, in compliance with the recommendations of the JPC, the Ministry of 
Health and Family Welfare has taken the following steps:— 
1. The standards for soft drinks, that is, the carbonated water have been 
amended making it mandatory to use water conforming to st andards 
prescribed for Packaged Drinking Water under the Prevention of Food 
Adulteration Rules, 1955, in the manufacture 
312 

[10 August, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
of carbonated water. An amendmen t of the standards of carbonated 
water was issued vide Notification No. GSR 451(E) dated 15.7.2004 
which came into force on 12.10.2004. It is reiterated that water 
constitutes 86-92 per cent of the soft drink (carbonated water). 
2. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has set up a National 
Level Expert Committee to advise the Central Committee for 
Food Standards on the issue of  pesticide residues. The 
composition of this Committee is:— 
(i) Dr. N.K. Ganguly, Director General, Indian Council of Medical 
Research (ICMR), Chairman 
(ii) Dr. S.K. Khanna, (Retd.), Industrial Toxicology Research Centre (ITRC), 
Lucknow 
(iii) Dr. N.P. Agnihotri, (Retd.), Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), 
New Delhi 
(iv) Dr. G. Thyagrajan, Ex-Directo r, Indian Institute of Chemical 
Technology, Hyderabad. 
The terms of reference of this Committee are as follows:— 
(i) To guide the Pesticide Residue Sub-Committee in fixation of 
Maximum Residual Limits (MRLs) of pesticides in carbonated 
beverages, fruits and vegetable juices and other finished products. 
(ii) To guide the pesticide Residue Sub-Committee on technical aspects 
of fixing MRLs including methodology toxicity, processing factor, method 
of analysis, health risks that may be considered for risk analysis, risk 
management and risk communication as per Codex Working 
Principles; 
(iii) To guide on monitoring of pesticides in carbonated beverages and 
other food commodities; 
(iv) To guide on any other matter on which pesticide residues sub-
committee, CCFS, Department of Health may require technical 
clarification/guidance. 
3. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has also requested 
the Ministry of Agriculture to provide the requisite residue data in 
313 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2006] 
respect of all pesticides registered for use of sugarcane to enable the 
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to notify Maximum Residue 
Limits (MRLs) in respect of these pesticides. In order to reduce the time 
taken to fix MRLs, my Ministry has streamlined the process of fixation 
of MRLs. 
4.  The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare commissioned a pilot study 
of sugar samples in September, 2005, in order to establish the 
methodology of sampling and testing for the same. The report of this 
study has been received. The pilot study of 200 sugar samples 
collected from retail and wholesale outlets as well as sugar factories 
from all regions of the country was entrusted to Bidhan Chandra 
Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya, (BCKW) Mohanpur, Kolkata which is part of 
the All India Coordinated Project on Pesticides. This pilot study 
broadly found absence of pesticide residues in the samples collected 
and tested. The data generated by the BCKW is being reviewed by a peer 
group of 2-3 Pesticides residues Chemists from the Government 
institutions/universities, which have been designated by the National 
Level Expert Committee. The peer review process is expected to be 
completed shortly. Based on the findings, it was decided by the 
Expert Committee to undertake a comprehensive multi-centre study 
using LC-MS-MS which is the most sophisticated equipment 
available so as to detect even the slightest traces of pesticides and 
conducted to pre-empt the remotest  possibility of even traces of 
pesticides through sugar. The study will be carried out by Bidhan 
Chandra Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya, the National Institute of 
Occupational Health and the National  Institute of Nutrition. The 
National Institute of Occupational Health, Ahmedabad, and the National 
Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad have since taken necessary steps to 
augment their facilities and have installed LC-MS-MS. 
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare views the issue of 
contamination of soft drinks (carbonated water) with utmost seriousness and is 
committed to protecting the health of  the consumers and would take all 
necessary steps to ensure this.
